title: Kitagawa 2005 Experiment 1 · rear temporal order
citation: Kitagawa, N., Zampini, M., & Spence, C. (2005). Audiotactile interactions in near and far space. Experimental Brain Research, 166(3–4), 528–537.
notes: Eight blocks preserve the published temporal-order cell counts for auditory inspection. Earlobe stimulation and participant data collection are blocked.

participants.paired_test_note: The paper reports paired tests with 9 degrees of freedom. The reason for the difference from the recruited count is unreported.

apparatus.source: Two fixed loudspeaker positions 45° left and right of the rear axis, 20 cm from head center.
apparatus.sound: White-noise bursts, 9 ms, calibrated to 82 dBA at the head.

published_trial_schedule.sign_rule: Sound onset minus tactile onset. Negative values indicate sound-first trials.

response.device: Hand-held two-key response pad operated with the thumbs.

analysis.primary_measure: Temporal-order judgment. Fit the normal-score transform of touch-first proportions separately by participant and side alignment.

inspection_scope.auditory_spatialization: Toolkit stereo pan; rear-left / rear-right placement is reported apparatus geometry.
inspection_scope.details: Digital, stationary sound bursts and nominal order combinations only. The touch side and lead are annotations; there is no tactile output, independent masker, fixation-light hardware or response scoring. Auditory onset is scheduled from an implicit fixation at the row start. The toolkit SOA control measures a nonnegative delay from sound onset. Touch-first timing remains a planned value.

implementation_gaps: The trial scheduler requires independent auditory and tactile triggers for signed temporal orders plus light feedback. This profile schedules only the auditory member of each pair.
Speaker and tactile calibration must verify delivered intensity and acoustic-to-skin onset. Original waveform bytes and measured timing are unavailable.

The original hand-held choice pad, fixation feedback and two-site electrical stimulator are required for response capture and tactile delivery. The reported voltage is a source record and cannot establish delivered current or calibration.

provenance.field: Rear geometry, source burst, electrocutaneous earlobe stimulation and tactile calibration
Signed timing, practice, trial counts, response and temporal-order fit
provenance.source: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00221-005-2393-8, pp. 529–531, Experiment 1 Methods, Results and Table 1.
